title: Incommensurate modulation with $Q=0$ A-type Antiferromagnetic Order in CeRh$_2$As$_2$ revealed by NQR studies
authors: Shiki Ogata, Shunsaku Kitagawa, Kenji Ishida, Manuel Brando, Elena Hassinger, Christoph Geibel, Seunghyun Khim
abstract: We performed $^{75}$As nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on a higher-quality single-crystalline CeRh$_2$As$_2$, a heavy-fermion superconductor exhibiting multiple superconducting (SC) phases under magnetic fields along the $c$ axis. This SC multiphase is believed to originate from staggered Rashba spin-orbit coupling associated with locally broken inversion symmetry. In addition to superconductivity, CeRh$_2$As$_2$ exhibits phase I below $T_0\sim0.5$ K and an antiferromagnetic (AFM) state below $T_{N}\sim 0.25$ K in the early-stage samples. In the higher-quality sample, the AFM transition becomes more pronounced, and $T_{N}$ increases to nearly coincide with $T_{SC}$. The NQR spectra at the As(1) site imply an internal field with an incommensurate distribution, indicating a two-dimensional incommensurate modulation of the magnetic structure superimposed on a $Q=0$ A-type AFM component. Moreover, a pronounced decrease in the NQR intensity at $T_0$ well-above $T_{N}$ and an abrupt increase in the internal field at $T_{N}$ suggest the emergence of a slowly fluctuating AFM order at $T_0$ which becomes static at $T_{N}$.
summary: This work uses NQR/NMR measurements on CeRh2As2 to characterize its magnetic state. The findings reveal a complex magnetic structure involving both A-type antiferromagnetism and an incommensurate modulation. Crucially, the study establishes a strong link between this magnetic ordering and the superconducting phase, suggesting that magnetism plays a pivotal role in the material's electronic properties.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature of magnetic order (A-type Antiferromagnetism) and its interplay with superconductivity in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2.
main_result: NQR studies reveal that the magnetic structure is a combination of a Q=0 A-type AFM component overlaid by a two-dimensional incommensurate modulation. The close proximity of the AFM transition temperature (TN) to the superconducting transition temperature (TSC) is highlighted.
method: The research employs high-quality single-crystal measurements using Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy on the As site.
model_or_system: The physical system is CeRh2As2, a heavy-fermion superconductor with a noncentrosymmetric crystal structure. The magnetic state is modeled as having both a Q=0 A-type AFM component and an incommensurate modulation.
key_observables: NQR spectral splitting (at As(2)), NQR intensity evolution, internal magnetic field strength (H_int), and the temperature dependence of these quantities near T0 and TN.
important_parameters: Superconducting transition temperature (T_SC), Antiferromagnetic transition temperature (T_N), and fluctuation onset temperature (T_0).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed magnetic transitions are robust features of the material, though early-stage sample inhomogeneity is noted as a limitation.
figures_summary: Figures compare NQR spectra between different crystal quality samples; others show the temperature evolution of spectral features and internal fields across multiple transition points (T0, TN, TSC).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by characterizing the superconducting phases, then analyzing the magnetic transitions using NQR/NMR data. It establishes the coexistence of incommensurate modulation on top of A-type AFM order, linking these magnetic features to the SC state.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between magnetism and superconductivity, particularly the observation that the onset of static AFM order coincides with or immediately follows the superconducting transition, is a key topic in strongly correlated electron physics relevant to unconventional superconductors.
